name: Cooper City
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Cooper City, FL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Cooper City, FL: Light Up Cooper City at Memorial Park, Cookies and Cocoa with Santa and the fire truck Santa program.
lede: Cooper City keeps Christmas close to home: a park lighting night with Santa's arrival, cookies and cocoa at the Community Center and Santa visiting neighborhoods on a fire truck.
celebrates: The City of Cooper City Parks and Recreation Department organizes the town's holiday season. Light Up Cooper City lights Memorial Park with community performances, craft vendors, food vendors and the arrival of Santa Claus. Cookies and Cocoa with Santa at the Community Center offers crafts and pictures with Santa for a fee, with registration through the city. The city also runs a Gingerbread House Decorating Contest and a Holiday Home Decorating Contest, and the Broward Sheriff's Office Fire Rescue sponsors a Holiday Santa Program in which Santa and his elves visit resident families by fire truck.
lastyear: In 2025 the city planned Light Up Cooper City for Friday, December 5, from 6:30 to 9 pm at Memorial Park. The day before, the city published a Know Before You Go notice with parking and shuttle service information and road closure details, and it asked people arriving by golf cart to use designated parking areas. The notice promised an evening filled with lights, music and community cheer to kick off the season.
facts: Cooper City is named for Morris Cooper, whose dream of a well-zoned community came about in 1959. By the end of that year, 85 residents lived in 35 completed homes. The land was once Wacico Groves, short for the Walsh Citrus Company, and the caretaker's home and packing house stood near the current Cooper City entrance on Griffin Road. Early settlers in the area farmed, raised livestock and grew oranges.
trains: Cooper City does not have its own Tri-Rail station. Tri-Rail's Broward stops include Sheridan Street at 2900 Sheridan Street in Hollywood and the Fort Lauderdale Airport station at 500 Gulf Stream Way in Dania. Metrorail and Metromover run in Miami-Dade County. Kids who love trains can ride the fire truck instead: the Holiday Santa Program brings Santa and his elves to Cooper City homes aboard a fire truck. For a bigger train day, the Gold Coast Railroad Museum in Miami has over 40 historic rail cars, including the Presidential Rail Car Ferdinand Magellan and Florida East Coast Steam Locomotive #153.

kidfact: Cooper City used to be an orange grove called Wacico Groves, short for the Walsh Citrus Company. Today the same land is a town with parks and neighborhoods.
faq: Where is the Cooper City tree lighting?

Light Up Cooper City happens at Memorial Park, 9001 SW 51st Street. The City of Cooper City describes it as an annual celebration with community performances, holiday craft vendors, food vendors, sounds of the season and the arrival of Santa Claus. Call 954-434-4300 extension 3 for details.
Can Santa visit my house in Cooper City?

The BSO Cooper City Holiday Santa Program sends Santa and his elves to resident families on a fire truck. Sign-up was open only to Cooper City residents, took place online and costs $15 per child, with proceeds supporting a scholarship program at Cooper City High School. The city says all available visits have been taken.
Are there events at the Cooper City Community Center?

Yes. The city holds Cookies and Cocoa with Santa at the Community Center, 9000 SW 50th Place, with crafts and pictures with Santa. The fee is $15 per child and $20 per adult, and registration is online, at the Community Center or at the Pool and Tennis Center.
Does Cooper City have decorating contests?

Yes. The city's special events page lists a Gingerbread House Decorating Contest and a Holiday Home Decorating Contest. Each costs $5 to enter, and the city lists the registration dates and the places to register on its special events page.
How did Cooper City get its name?

The city is named for Morris Cooper, whose dream of a well-zoned community came about in 1959. According to the City of Cooper City, by the end of that year 85 residents lived within 35 completed homes, and early residents worked on street lights, paved streets and arrangements for mail and a school.
